actual_import: Every scalar finite Gel'fand-Dikii string combination with arbitrary constant lower flows has sectorial spectral fundamental matrices with the displayed fixed formal phase and constant right Stokes matrices.
The original string companion spectral system has an ordinary origin after the cubic spectral pullback; no generic Fuchsian nonresonance hypothesis is needed there.
Scalar string solutions with matching phase and right Stokes matrices are locally identical.
hypotheses_checked: Normalized scalar leading operator is monic of order3 with quadratic coefficient zero.
Highest effective flow m is not divisible by3, so the leading irregular matrix J^m has three distinct eigenvalues; its nonzero coefficient is constant.
Every lower flow is a constant coefficient in a finite linear combination, exactly as allowed by the page43 remark.
All compared coefficient branches are holomorphic on a common local time domain; their normalized formal phases match.
Algebraic continuation supplies another local branch, avoiding any need for global inverse-data existence or genericity.
primary_source.excluded_use: No application of Theorem9.5 to arbitrary or degenerate inverse data and no meromorphic scalar reconstruction from a general resonant connection family.

new_written_arguments: Finite leading-order subtraction writes any cubic mate as a sum of positive fractional powers plus a commuting polynomial.
The negative fractional-power coefficients give x=-3*r2/kappa with x'=1 before analytic arguments.
Formal phase coefficients lie in the algebraic coefficient field and have zero time derivative except the fixed xzJ term, so they cannot change upon algebraic continuation.

The correctly oriented left ratio Psi_tilde*Psi^-1 cancels right Stokes jumps. Its entire spectral behavior and Lambda_z growth give a unipotent lower triangular polynomial; first-row equality and time derivatives identify the scalar operators.
Finite algebraic branch continuation preserves the phase and Stokes matrices, so scalar injectivity excludes every finite branch, including pole branching.

The dispersionless residue polynomial is a monomial of exponents at most1 times simple nonzero binary factors; a finite Pfaff transformation reduces this to Jacobi polynomials with alpha,beta greater than-1.
Jacobi root simplicity is justified directly by Rodrigues orthogonality and a sign-change argument.
Derivative weights and the two leading gradient invariants contradict rational infinity for every effective m>=2 coprime to3, retaining all lower flows.
Prescribed regular Long reductions of orders2 and3 are incompatible with the resulting arbitrary-order cubic mate normal form.

Arbitrary characteristic-zero constants descend through a finite d/dx-stable field F0/k0(x), with k0 finitely generated, followed by base change to C(x) and a field component; x stays transcendental and the restriction to F0 remains injective.
orientation_note: The Section8 presentation has inconsistent ratio orientations. The current written proof uses the left ratio required for equal right jumps, and independently derives its first-row consequence.
checker_scope: Finite exact controls support the algebraic formulas and terminating identities. They do not replay Stokes existence/injectivity, analytic continuation, or all-order Jacobi root simplicity.
remaining_scope: Generic scalar order>=4, nonpositional first images and nonscalar carriers remain open. No DC1/DC2 solution or bounded Long construction is claimed.
